key_insight: AgentSSL shows that MLE agents can adapt semi-supervised learning techniques to exploit unlabeled data, but selecting the best generated program remains a major bottleneck.
engineering_relevance: Agent-designed SSL pipelines could reduce manual engineering and labeling demands in data-scarce domains, provided program selection is reliable.
method: Frame semi-supervised learning as a program search problem under limited supervision.
Evaluate agent-generated SSL pipelines under weak feedback and matched compute.
Benchmark unsupervised and active program selection with ProgramSelectBench.
evidence_signal: Agents exceeded the strongest human-engineered baselines in 8 of 12 settings by up to +21.8%; ProgramSelectBench contains 16,977 agent-generated and human-engineered SSL programs.
watch_item: Selection using the agent's feedback metric caused performance drops of up to 47%, and transfer to real-world ecology detection remains challenging.
paper_title: AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?
